clue.text: Letters many tear up, in a way

indicators.note: the pieces for 'many' and 'tear up' are placed inside the word for 'a way'

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to tear up a sheet is to rip it

explanation.surface: Somebody describes the letters that many people rip up in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C and RIP inside ST, the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting or a set of written characters is called a script, so letters in that sense fit.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of rig are put out of order

explanation.surface: A dog turns up in a suit of corporate work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes RGI from RIG, after CO. 'rig-out' looks like one word meaning outfit, but it splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a dog, and the corgi is one breed of dog.

clue.text: Means to enter faulty item without delay

indicators.note: the word for 'Means' goes into the scrambled letters, entering them
faulty signals that the letters of item are wrongly arranged

parts.note: media are means of communication, plural of medium

explanation.surface: A method for getting a defective item in straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' turns ITEM into IMTE, and 'to enter' puts MEDIA inside it: IM-MEDIA-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at once, with nothing put off, is the sense of instant.

clue.text: Subject is about right for a worldly circle

indicators.note: the word for 'Subject' goes about, i.e. around, the letter for right

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic

explanation.surface: A theme is said to be suitable for a sophisticated social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts TOPIC round R. 'worldly circle' is a line of latitude on the globe, not a sophisticated set of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude circling the earth.

explanation.surface: Somebody is booking a reserved match for a group of tennis players.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, a set is part of a match, so a tie between sides can be pictured as a set aside: a set played by each side.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to put it by for later; read cryptically, a set between sides is a tennis contest.

explanation.surface: A comment that dodging work is a reasonable way to go about things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors once measured depth by swinging a lead weight on a line, so 'sound' here means taking soundings; the idiom for shirking comes from that easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirking by feigning illness is the idiom's meaning; heaving the plumb weight to measure the depth of water is its literal one.

explanation.surface: Negotiation might smooth over resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-feeling' reads as resentment, but the second sense is a doctor dealing with a patient's sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Negotiating terms is one sense; giving medical care that cures illness is the other.

parts.note: stories read as tales but mean floors of a building, joined by one step of a flight

explanation.surface: A bridge passage that joins two narratives.
explanation.definitionFit: Floors of a house are joined by steps, each a single tread in the climb from one level to the next.

clue.text: Detracts from position of nobleman in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the nobleman's title is placed in the name of the Norfolk town

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone takes away from a nobleman's standing in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, an English county; 'in' signals the container and 'from position of' only links. 'Detracts' is a verb: discounts as in disregards.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard or play down something reduces its value, so the verb means takes away from.

clue.text: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it

definitions.text: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it

parts.words: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it
parts.note: bound means a leap, not certain: an acrobat's jump is sent upward by the springy apparatus

explanation.surface: An artist is sure to be inspired by something.
explanation.definitionFit: The springy canvas sheet on a frame throws a gymnast's leap into the air.

indicators.note: filling signals letters found inside the words meals ordinarily

explanation.surface: A remark that the usual meals are rather too filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' looks like an adjective about meals, but it signals the run inside 'meals, ordinarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Too in the sense of in addition is a synonym of as well.

explanation.surface: Someone is cheating while providing musical accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddling means cheating, and also playing the violin, which supplies musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating on accounts is one sense; playing a violin, whose music is made of notes, is the other.

indicators.note: the word for the lake holds the river's name inside it

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A lake has a river fish living in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts PO inside TARN. 'river fish' reads as one phrase, but the river is a piece and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large silvery game species of warm Atlantic waters is known by this name.

explanation.surface: A large flightless bird is worshipped as a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhea is the Titan goddess, mother of Zeus, and also a large flightless South American bird resembling an ostrich.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American flightless bird is a ratite like an ostrich; the Titaness was mother of the Olympians.

clue.text: So dry that we resort to a kind of water-diviner?

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort: the letters of so dry that are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: It is so arid that people turn to a dowser to find water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, rearranging SO DRY THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument detects or regulates water, a mechanical stand-in for a dowser.

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

indicators.note: back signals the word for cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: A number is scaled back and cut from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal. Ninepins is skittles, a bowling game played by knocking down standing pins.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles played with nine upright pins is a pub bowling game.

clue.text: Man of action joins ugly quarrel

parts.note: plain is a polite word for unattractive
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A man of deeds gets caught up in a nasty argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' means a lawsuit: the man of action is the party who sues.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who brings a lawsuit is the party who starts legal proceedings.

clue.text: Dry letter written to L.T.A. members

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

indicators.note: members read as the parts of L.T.A., taken apart and put back together in another order

explanation.surface: A temperance note is posted to people in the tennis association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' rearranges the letters of L.T.A. as TAL. The L.T.A. is the Lawn Tennis Association, the body that runs British tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry in the sense of abstaining from alcohol describes someone who never drinks.

clue.text: Supporter, gives a hand, tree chopping

indicators.note: chopping signals the letters of hand and tree are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A follower lends a hand by felling a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping' rearranges HAND and TREE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a cause or leader is one who sticks to it.

clue.text: Recess in which leaders of all parties save extremists meet

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the four words all parties save extremists

explanation.surface: A place where heads of every party except the radicals get together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save extremists' looks like it means excluding the extremes, but each word just gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular recess at the end of a church is the architectural term.

clue.text: Amatory upset? It is heart breaking!

indicators.note: is here means is set in: the upturned word sits inside the broken heart
breaking signals the word for heart is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the core of something is its heart

indicators.note: upset in a down clue signals the word It is turned upside down

explanation.surface: A lover is distressed and cries that it is heartbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IT into TI; 'breaking' makes EROC from CORE; 'is' puts TI inside: ERO-TI-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes sexual love, and so does the word for arousing desire.

indicators.note: last tells us that the word at is placed at the end, after the crest

parts.note: a comb is the red crest on a cockerel's head

explanation.surface: A combat at the summit at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' reads as finally, but 'last' only places the second piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight between armed forces is a battle.

explanation.surface: A fiddler plays in a garden shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A violinist draws a bow, so is a bow-er, and a bower is a leafy shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler wields a bow; a shady leafy retreat in a garden is the other sense.

parts.note: Don Quixote roamed as a knight seeking adventure, which is the life this word names

explanation.surface: An idealistic job.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights of romance wandered in search of adventures, the business Don Quixote took up.

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for organ piece is said out loud

parts.note: a reed is a vibrating part of some organ pipes

explanation.surface: A writer listened to a piece of organ music.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of 'The Cloister and the Hearth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist.

explanation.surface: Somebody tidied away a few letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five letters' reads as a count of the word's length, but S TO W runs S, T, U, V, W: five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing items into storage is one sense; read as 'S to W', the second spans five letters of the alphabet.

indicators.note: variety signals a varied arrangement of chit a later

explanation.surface: A flashy note is sent out later as a sort of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges CHIT, A and LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated and dramatic behaviour is called theatrical, as though staged.

clue.text: Surprised to have begun taking in money

indicators.note: the word for begun takes the money letter inside it

parts.note: started means having begun
L is the abbreviation for pound, i.e. money

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find cash coming in so early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts L (librum, the pound) inside STARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping in alarm at something unexpected is being astonished.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the bronchial type is spoken out loud

parts.note: someone with a bronchial complaint is a cougher

explanation.surface: Someone describes a chest with lung trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' reads as the body part, given 'bronchial', but it is a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox for keeping valuables is a chest.
